questions.question: The kingdoms of Chola, Chera and Pandyas belong to which period in the ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangam Period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sangam Age, sometimes referred to as the Tamil Sangam period, was an important period in South India's history. It is generally believed that the Sangam era occurred between 300 BCE and 300 CE.
 
• Three dynasties—the Chera, Chola, and Pandyas—ruled the Tamil nation during the Sangam Period. They were Muvendar, jointly as well.
 
• For administrative convenience, the kingdom was split into the following divisions: Mandalam (territory), Nadu (province), Ur (town), Perur (large village), and Sirur (small village).
 
• More terms used in sangam age:
 
 
• Karai: Land tax 
 
• Ulgu: Customs duties
 
• Iravu: Forced gift/extra demand 
 
• Irai: Tribute paid by feudatories 
 
• Variyar: Tax collector
 
• Vanigar: Traders and Merchants
 
• Arasar: Ruling Class
 
• Vellalars: Dominant Agricultural caste
 
• Uzhavars: Middle-class Agricultural caste
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Mauryan Period:

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He is referred to in Greek sources as Sandrokottos.
 
• In 321 BC, he defeated Dhana Nanda and took the throne with the aid of a politically astute and clever Brahmin named Kautilya.
 
• Megasthenes served as the Greek representative in the court of Chandragupta.
 
• He led an expansionist policy that subjugated nearly all of modern-day India, except a few isolated areas in the far south and Kalinga.
 
• Bindusara is the second Mauryan Empire ruler.
 
• 297–273 BC was his rule period.
 
• He was also called Amitraghata (Slayer of foes).
 
• Ashoka mentions in his inscription that he conquered Kalinga after becoming the king for eight years.
 
• Kalinga was a region located in present-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Ashoka established Ujjain and Takshashila (later Taxila) as the regional capitals of his kingdom.
 
 
 
• **Mahajanapada period:**
 
 
• **​**In **Jambudipa (Bharatvarsha)**, there were **sixteen **republics of significant size and authority known as **"Solasa Mahajanapada**," according to the **Buddhist **canonical scripture** Anguttara Nikaya**.
 
• The sixteen Mahajanapadas belonged to either a **republican or monarchical political structure**.
 
• The republics were located in present-day Punjab in northwest India and along the foothills of the Himalayas, while the monarchies were primarily located in the Gangetic Plains.
 
• They existed from the** 6th to 4th century BCE**.
 
• The **Anguttara Nikaya** lists **sixteen Mahajanapadas**, and they are:

questions.question: The Amaravati School of art was developed under the patronage of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satavahanas.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Amaravati School of art was developed under the patronage of Satavahanas, who ruled over the Andhra region from the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
 
• The school of art is known for its distinctive style of sculpture, characterized by intricate details, delicate features, and graceful postures. 
 
• The sculptures of the Amaravati School were primarily made from limestone, and they depicted scenes from the life of Buddha, Jataka tales, and other Buddhist themes.
 
• The Amaravati Stupa, located in present-day Andhra Pradesh, is one of the most significant examples of the school's art and architecture, and it is considered a masterpiece of Buddhist art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Palas were known for their patronage of Buddhism and the arts, but they were based in present-day Bengal and Bihar, far away from the Andhra region.**
 
• The Cheras and Cholas were primarily Tamil dynasties and did not have a significant presence in the Andhra region, where the Amaravati School flourished.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of six school of Indian Philosophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravida.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dravida** is not a school of Indian philosophy.
 
• Dravida is a term used to refer to the** southern part of India.**
 
• **Samkhya** is one of the **oldest schools of Indian philosophy** that focuses on the** dualism of matter and spirit.**
 
• It believes in the existence of **Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter)** and their interplay.
 
• **Yoga** is a school of Indian philosophy that emphasizes the practice of **physical, mental, and spiritual disciplines** to attain liberation or Moksha.
 
• It is based on the** Yoga Sutras of Patanjali.**
 
• **Nyaya **is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on** logic and reasoning.**
 
• It aims to establish the validity of** knowledge and perception **through inference and deduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian philosophy** is a vast field that encompasses various schools of thought, each with its unique approach and philosophy.
 
• The six schools of Indian philosophy are **Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. **
 
• **Vaisheshika** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on **metaphysics and epistemology.**
 
• It believes in the** existence of atoms** and their combination to form matter.
 
• **Mimamsa** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the interpretation of** Vedic texts and rituals.**
 
• It aims to establish the correct meaning and purpose of the** Vedic texts.**
 
• **Vedanta** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the **Upanishads **and the concept of the **ultimate reality or Brahman.**
 
• It emphasizes the unity of the individual self or **Atman with Brahman.**

questions.question: In the context of Gupta administration, the term 'vithi' referred to a/an:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**administrative unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the context of the Gupta administration, the term 'this' referred to the administrative unit**__.
 
• In ** Gupta Empire**, the king was directed in his administration by a community and group consisting of a chief minister and a Senapati.
 
 
• There were various names of the Empire "**Rajya", Rashtra", "Desha", "Mandala", "Prithvi", and "Avani**".
 
• The Empire was divided into provinces called Bhukti, Bhoga, and Pradesh.
 
• **Provinces further divided into "Vishayas" and came under the control of persons called "Vishaya Patis**".
 
• "Vishaya" further divided into "Nagaras" and "Nagares" were divided into villages. "Vithi” was a part of “Vishaya".
 
• A group or collection of villages was called "Pethaka" and "Santaka".
 
• Smaller units of a village were "**Agrahara" and "Patta**".
 
• A **Sandivigraha** was the minister for foreign affairs.
 
• They were mentioned in the **Gupta inscriptions. **
 
• Bhuktis was the name of Provinces in the Gupta Empire.
 
• **Uparikas** was the name of provincial governors.
 
• The king maintained deep contact with the provincial administration. By a group of officials called Kumaramatyas and Ayuktas.

questions.question: Which Turkish invader attacked and raided the temple of Somnath in 1025 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahmud Ghazni.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Turkish invader **Mahmud Ghazni**, attacked and **raided **the temple of **Somnath in 1025 AD**.
 
• The first of India's twelve sacred jyotirlingas is said to have arisen at the elaborately carved honey-colored Somnath temple or Deo Patan, is located in Prabhas Patan, Veraval in Gujarat, India.
 
 
• It is said that Shiva manifested there as a blazing column of light.
 
• The temples are situated where the Sarasvati, Hiran, and Kapila rivers converge, and the shoreline where they are built is touched by the ebb and flow of the Arabian Sea.
 
• Although the timeline of the ancient temple starts in 649 BC, it is thought to be older.
 
• Though it's difficult to see them through the foggy glass, vibrant dioramas depicting the Shiva narrative border the north side of the temple grounds.
 
• The temple was reconstructed several times in the past after repeated destruction by multiple Muslim invaders and rulers, notably starting with an attack by Mahmud Ghazni in the 11th century.
 
 
• The Pran-Pratistha at the existing temple was done on 11th May 1951 by then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Yamin ad-Dawlah** In the province of Ghazna, **Mahmud ibn** **Sebuktigin **was born on November 2, 971.

 
 
• He **founded **the **Turkic Ghaznavid dynasty,** which ruled from 998 to 1030.
 
• By the time of his death, his domain had grown into a vast military empire that included Khwarazm in Transoxiana, Punjab in India, Makran, and northwest Iran itself.
 
• Famous **Poet **Patronized by Mahmud Ghazni were **Firdausi **who wrote **Shahnameh **and **Alberuni **who wrote **Kitab-i-hind.**
 
• Mahmud **invaded Gujarat **in **1025**, plundering the **Somnath shrine **and destroying its jyotirlinga. His loot included 2 million dinars. Somnath was conquered, and Anhilwara was invaded as retaliation.
 
 
 
• **Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad**, also called **Muhammad of Ghor**, ruled the **Ghurid Empire** as its lone ruler from **1202 to 1206**, having served as its sultan from 1173 to 1202.
 
 
• He is credited with bringing about centuries-long **Muslim hegemony on the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• Originating from Persia, Muhammad Ghori reigned over portions of what is now Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq (MBT)** was the son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, also known as **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**, who **founded the Tughlaq dynasty** by subduing the Delhi Sultanate. 
 
 
• Other names for him are **Ulugh Khan** and **Prince Fakhr Malik Jauna Khan**.
 
• The Deccan region of India, which is now Maharashtra, is home to **Daulatabad**, also called **Devagiri**, and it was Tughluq who **ordered the relocation of his capital from Delhi.**
 
• He introduced **token money** in the form of brass and copper coins with a par value with gold and silver coins.

questions.question: Four ashrams were recognised by Brahmins around the time when Jainism and Buddhism were becoming popular. Which of the following was NOT a recognised ashrama?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parmarth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Parmarth was **not** a recognised ashrama.
 
• The four recognised ashramas were **Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Brahmacharya, and Sannyasa.**
 
• These ashramas were recognised by Brahmins as stages of life that an individual would pass through in order to attain spiritual growth and enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Grihastha was the householder stage, where an individual would get married and fulfill their worldly duties.
 
• Vanaprastha was the retirement stage, where an individual would withdraw from worldly affairs and focus on spiritual pursuits.
 
• Brahmacharya was the student stage, where an individual would study under a guru and learn the scriptures.
 
• Sannyasa was the renunciate stage, where an individual would renounce all worldly possessions and dedicate themselves completely to spiritual pursuits.

questions.question: Who among the following was the famous ruler of the Gauda Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shashanka** was the first historical ruler of the Gauda Kingdom, located in present-day Bengal.
 
• He ruled from approximately **590 CE to 625 CE**, and his reign marked the emergence of Bengal as a significant political power.
 
• Shashanka is credited with the **establishment of a unified kingdom in Bengal** and was one of the earliest known kings to embrace Hinduism in the region.
 
• He is often associated with the persecution of Buddhists, including the alleged destruction of the Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya, though this remains a debated topic among historians.
 
• Shashanka's rivalry with **Harsha**, the ruler of Kannauj, is well-documented in historical texts, including the accounts of the Chinese traveler Xuanzang.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gauda Kingdom:**

 
 
• The Gauda Kingdom was an early medieval kingdom centered in Bengal, particularly in the western and northern parts of the region.
 
• It played a critical role in shaping the political and cultural landscape of early medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Harsha:**
 
 
• Harsha was a contemporary of Shashanka and ruled northern India from 606 CE to 647 CE.
 
• He expanded his kingdom significantly but was unable to annex the Gauda Kingdom due to Shashanka's resistance.
 
 
 
• **Xuanzang’s Accounts:**
 
 
• The Chinese traveler Xuanzang visited India during the reign of Harsha and documented the political and cultural dynamics of the time.
 
• He mentioned Shashanka's rule in Bengal and his alleged hostility towards Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Shashanka:**
 
 
• Shashanka is considered a pivotal figure in the history of Bengal, as he laid the foundation for subsequent kingdoms in the region.
 
• His rule marked the beginning of Bengal's prominence in the political history of India.
